findings.source_quote: ἐὰν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος ἐπισκέψασθαι τὸν πύργον
findings.english_quote: If the master comes to inspect the tower
findings.issue: The independent title κύριος is rendered “master” rather than the project's prescribed reader-facing “Lord.” The contextual explanation in note c identifies the referent's role but does not establish a source-based necessity for departing from that title policy.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose “If the Lord comes to inspect the tower,” with a revised note explaining the tower owner's role and distinguishing this title from the respectful address to the shepherd. Review that replacement before adoption.

findings.source_quote: τῶν ἠρμένων καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν βεβλημένων
findings.english_quote: “Removed and put into the building” follows Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture compared with Latin Vulgata. Reported Athos has a differently ordered “fitted into the building and” phrase; the other versions are uncertain in the apparatus.
findings.issue: The selected Greek supports the English working reading, but the supplied evidence does not contain the relevant apparatus entry or a bounded report establishing the named conjecture, the Athos wording, or the uncertainty of the other versions. The note presents those specific textual-history claims as established without identifying supporting evidence available in this review.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected working reading. Supply an attributed apparatus transcription or comparison report with a locator supporting these claims, or explicitly label the unsupported details as unverified earlier editorial reports pending clarification.

findings.english_quote: “The work will soon be finished” follows the printed working choice compared with the versions. The corresponding Athos word is reported illegible, with a completion suggesting a related finishing verb. It is not a fully legible unanimous Greek reading.
findings.issue: The translation faithfully represents the selected clause, but the supplied comparison report does not establish the claimed Athos illegibility, proposed completion, or comparison with the versions. These are specific apparatus claims, not conclusions that can be drawn from the selected Greek alone.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide the relevant attributed apparatus excerpt or bounded report. Otherwise retain the working translation while qualifying these details as unverified prior reports; do not imply fresh inspection of Athos handwriting.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα [πάντα] μοι ἐπιλύσῃ ἃ ἔδειξέ μοι.
findings.english_quote: The first “everything” translates a bracketed insertion by Harmer compared with the Latin traditions and Ethiopic; Athos is reported to omit it.
findings.issue: The source visibly brackets πάντα, and the note correctly distinguishes it from unbracketed text. However, the supplied evidence does not establish the attribution to Harmer, the stated version support, or the reported Athos omission. Those additional provenance claims exceed what the supplied source and reports demonstrate.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep disclosure that the first “everything” represents bracketed editorial text in the selected working source. Supply a located apparatus report for the attribution and witness claims, or mark those details as unverified earlier editorial reporting. Retain the separately disclosed uncertainty about the following Athos clause.

findings.source_quote: Ὕπαγε καὶ φέρε ἄσβεστον καὶ ὄστρακον λεπτόν
findings.english_quote: Bring lime and finely crushed pottery.
findings.issue: The simplified edition omits the separate command Ὕπαγε, “Go.” Bringing the materials may imply movement, but it does not explicitly preserve both commands in the selected source.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose “Go and bring lime and finely crushed pottery.” Review the revised sentence against the source before adoption.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἠρξάμην αὐτὸν ὁρκίζειν κατὰ τοῦ Κυρίου
findings.english_quote: and solemnly begged him by the Lord
findings.issue: The simplified edition drops ἠρξάμην, which explicitly says the narrator began the adjuration. This is a source event marker, not merely a feature of the standard edition's style.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose “and began solemnly begging him by the Lord,” or another accessible rendering that preserves both the beginning and the solemn appeal by the Lord. Review the replacement afresh.

findings.source_quote: ἐὰν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος ἐπισκέψασθαι τὸν πύργον
findings.english_quote: If the master comes to inspect the tower
findings.issue: The independent title κύριος is rendered “master” instead of the project's prescribed “Lord.” The explanation of the owner's role does not establish why the prescribed title cannot be retained.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose “If the Lord comes to inspect the tower,” and revise note c to explain the contextual role without replacing the reader-facing title. Review the replacement before adoption.

findings.source_quote: τῶν ἠρμένων καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν βεβλημένων
findings.english_quote: “Removed and put into the building” follows Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture compared with Latin Vulgata. Reported Athos has a differently ordered “fitted into the building and” phrase; the other versions are uncertain in the apparatus.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this note makes specific conjecture and witness claims not established by the supplied evidence. The selected source establishes the working wording but does not supply the apparatus needed to substantiate these attributions.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected working translation. Provide an attributed, located apparatus transcription or report, or qualify these details as unverified prior editorial reports rather than established comparisons.

findings.english_quote: “The work will soon be finished” follows the printed working choice compared with the versions. The corresponding Athos word is reported illegible, with a completion suggesting a related finishing verb. It is not a fully legible unanimous Greek reading.
findings.issue: The selected clause supports the translation, but no supplied apparatus excerpt or bounded comparison establishes the asserted Athos illegibility, completion, or version comparison. Copying the standard note does not independently substantiate those claims.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply the relevant attributed report with a locator, or explicitly qualify these details as unverified prior reports. Keep the selected reading and avoid implying fresh handwriting verification.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα [πάντα] μοι ἐπιλύσῃ ἃ ἔδειξέ μοι.
findings.english_quote: The first “everything” translates a bracketed insertion by Harmer compared with the Latin traditions and Ethiopic; Athos is reported to omit it.
findings.issue: The bracketed status of πάντα is supported and properly disclosed. Its attribution to Harmer and the specific supporting and omitting witnesses are not established in the supplied evidence.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the distinction between bracketed editorial text and unbracketed source text. Provide a located apparatus report for the remaining claims, or identify them as unverified earlier editorial reporting. Preserve the note's honest uncertainty about the following Athos clause.

summary: Both editions substantially preserve the selected working Greek, including necessity, the conditional inspection, strong negation, speaker relationships, and the virgins' companionship. Both require correction of the title-policy departure and better evidentiary qualification of specific apparatus claims. The simplified edition additionally omits the explicit command to go and the beginning of the adjuration. The bracketed supplement is disclosed, and the uncertain alternative to the occupation clause is appropriately left unresolved. These findings do not establish that the reported variants are false, authenticate unseen manuscripts, or justify replacing the selected working reading. All proposed English replacements require fresh review.
